/**
 * Provides static methods for generating keyboard template blocks from `LabelGKeyboard` definitions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This class generates HTML-like `<g-keyboard>` blocks for the template engine. Requires `LabelGKeyboard` to be set via {@link BlockGKeyboard.label} before using {@link BlockGKeyboard._build}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // blocks/g-keyboard.ts
 * import { BlockGKeyboard, LabelGKeyboard } from "gramstax";
 *
 * class KeyboardGBlock extends BlockGKeyboard {
 *   static label = class extends LabelGKeyboard {
 *     static backNext = {en: "Back, Next", id: "Kembali, Lanjut"}
 *   }
 *   static backNext = (lang?: string, type?: string) => this._build(`backNext`, lang, type)
 * }
 *
 * // base/page.ts
 * import {KeyboardGBlock} from "~/blocks/g-keyboard"
 * export abstract class PageBase extends CtxCore {
 *   static kbk = KeyboardGBlock
 *   static kbl = KeyboardGBlock.label
 * }
 *
 * // pages/some.ts
 * import {PageBase} from "~/base/page"
 * export class SomePage extends PageBase {
 *   static template = `
 *     <g-base>
 *       ${this.kbk.backNext()}
 *       <g-message>Default message hello world</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *     <g-base id="others-id-1">
 *       <g-message>Message from others id 1 with keyboard from base id default</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *     <g-base id="others-id-2">
 *       <g-base>${this.kbk.backNext()}</g-base>
 *       <g-message>Message from others id 3 with keyboard in same base</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *   `
 * }
 *
 * // understanding example
 * this.kbk.backNext() // will show all language with block template
 * this.kbk.backNext("id") // will show all language only (lang="id") with block template
 * this.kbk.backNext("default") // will show all language only (lang="default" or without lang) with block template
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Extends {@link https://github.com/jaredwray/keyv | Keyv} to provide a unified caching interface with built-in support for memory and Redis storage.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Storage modes: - **Memory mode:** when `url` is `"memory"` (default), uses an in-memory `Map`. - **Redis mode:** when `url` starts with `"redis"`, uses `@keyv/redis` adapter. - **Custom mode:** when `more.forceStore` is provided, uses the custom store.
 *
 * @typeParam V - The type of values stored in the cache.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { CacheExternal } from "gramstax";
 *
 * // Memory cache (default)
 * const memoryCache = new CacheExternal();
 *
 * // Redis cache
 * const redisCache = new CacheExternal("redis://localhost:6379", 3600000, "s");
 *
 * // With namespace and TTL
 * const cache = new CacheExternal("memory", 60000, "myapp");
 *
 * // Set and get data
 * await cache.set("user:123", { name: "John" });
 * const user = await cache.get("user:123");
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: CacheExternal

 * Refreshes the LRU cache by re-accessing keys in order.

 *
 * @param maxLength - Maximum number of keys to refresh. If omitted, refreshes all keys.

 */

 * `resolveMediaInput` returns a pre-built `InputFile` as-is when no `filename` is given; sharing that single instance across concurrent `send*` calls risks interleaved stream state. Broadcast paths wrap every resolved value with this helper (per recipient, inside the worker), so each send owns its copy. Non-`InputFile` values (`string` sources) pass through unchanged. The trailing `roots` param exists for call-site uniformity with `resolveMediaInput` and is intentionally ignored — cloning never re-evaluates the jail.
 *
 * @param value - Resolved media input (`string` or `InputFile`).
 *
 * @param _roots - Ignored; accepted so jail-forwarding call sites read uniformly.
 *
 * @returns A prototype-preserving shallow clone for `InputFile`, else `value` unchanged.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: cloneMediaInput

/**
 * Build `EphemeralMessageParameters` for Bot API 10.3 ephemeral messages.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Creates the `ephemeral_message_parameters` payload accepted by 13 send* methods plus `sendRichMessage`. Ephemeral messages are short-lived notifications sent directly to a user — they disappear after the user reads (or ignores) them and are not kept in the chat history.
 *
 * The deprecated shim also accepts the pre-10.3 snake_case object `{receiver_user_id, callback_query_id, ...}` and emits a `console.warn`.
 *
 * @param receiverUserId - Target user id, or a legacy object with snake_case keys.
 *
 * @param callbackQueryId - Callback query id that triggered the message (optional).

 * @param replace - Pass `true` to show in place of the original message (optional).
 *
 * @returns The ephemeral parameters object, or `undefined` when no receiver is provided.
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Replace callback query message in place
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   await this.api.sendMessage(this.chatId, `Order received!`, {
 *     ephemeral_message_parameters: this.ephemeralParams(this.from?.id, this.callbackQuery?.id, true)
 *   })
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Legacy 10.2 snake_case object (warns once)
 * ```typescript
 * this.ephemeralParams({receiver_user_id: 123, callback_query_id: `cb_1`})
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Page-level hook after a route handler execution.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Always runs after the handler returns (even when the handler returns undefined / null). Ideal for cleanup, analytics, or chained side effects.

 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Notify admins of high-value actions
 * async hookAfterRoute() {
 *   if (this.temp.session?.params.amount > 10000) {
 *     await this.api.sendMessage(ADMIN_CHAT_ID, `Large withdrawal: ${this.temp.session.amount}`)
 *   }
 * }
 * ```

 */
members.name: hookAfterRoute

members.docComment:
/**
 * Page-level hook before route handler execution.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Return `false` to **skip only the target route handler** (e.g. `handleFreeText`, `handleCallbackQueryData`, etc.). The rest of the framework is untouched — you can still call `.render()`, `.renderEdit()`, `.renderAnswerCallback()`, and other Ctx methods normally inside this hook before returning `false`.
 *
 * In other words: returning `false` does NOT freeze the page — it only prevents one specific handler from running.
 *
 * Useful for: - Per-page cooldown / rate limiting (reply "please wait" then abort) - Precondition checks (reply with redirect page then abort) - Session validity gates
 *
 * @returns `true` to continue (handler runs), `false` to abort (handler skipped).
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Cooldown — reply then abort the handler
 * async hookBeforeRoute() {
 *   const last = await this.cacheSession.get(`${this.from.id}:lastAction`)
 *   if (last && Date.now() - Number(last) < 2000) {
 *     await this.renderAnswerCallback(`Please wait...`) // still works
 *     return false // only skips the target handler
 *   }
 *   await this.cacheSession.set(`${this.from.id}:lastAction`, String(Date.now()))
 *   return true
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // KYC gate — send redirect page then abort
 * async hookBeforeRoute() {
 *   const profile = await this.db.getUser(this.from.id)
 *   if (!profile?.kycVerified) {
 *     await new KycPage(this).showForm() // redirect works
 *     return false // only skips the guarded handler
 *   }
 *   return true
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookBeforeRoute

/**
 * Posts a story on behalf of a managed business account.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Business-connection-only: a normal bot cannot call `postBusinessStory` — pass a `business_connection_id` from a `BusinessConnection` update with the `can_manage_stories` right, otherwise the Bot API rejects the call. Thin passthrough otherwise: `content` resolves through `resolveMedia` then uploads (`InputFile` as-is, URLs via `{url}`, `file_id` strings pass through) and only presence, the `photo`/`video` discriminant, and the fixed `active_period` set are fail-fast validated; areas, durations, and captions are adjudicated by the Bot API — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.
 *
 * why-not-base: explicit `businessConnectionId` (base `Context.postStory` uses the current update only) plus local-path `InputFile` resolution and fail-fast validation.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`). There is no degraded fallback content for stories, so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * @param businessConnectionId - Business connection id (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param content - Story content `{type: "photo"|"video", src}` (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param activePeriod - Archive delay in seconds: 21600, 43200, 86400, or 172800 (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param options - Optional extra story fields such as `caption` (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The posted story object.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handlePostStory() {
 *   await this.postBusinessStory(`conn-1`, {type: `photo`, src: `https://example.com/pic.jpg`}, 86400)
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: postBusinessStory

/**
 * Sends a message to multiple users in bulk.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Automatically throttles after 30 messages to respect Telegram rate limits. Uses each user's specified language code for template rendering. Per-recipient send failures follow `Ctx.classifySendError`: `retryable` errors are counted and the loop continues; `fallback-text` errors additionally trigger a best-effort fallback-text send to that recipient (nested failures ignored). `failedCount`/`firstError` semantics are preserved either way; loop structure and pacing are untouched. Retryable failures (`429`/`5xx`/network) never abort the run: they are recorded in `retryable` (absolute `index` + `id` + `error`, completion order) while the checkpoint keeps advancing, so callers can re-drive just those entries with a fresh pass. `firstError` stays the first failure of any kind. Checkpoint-first (anti-spam over speed): `startFrom` resumes after a restart without resending (indexes below count as skipped, `done` in `onProgress` counts processed recipients, `total` is `ids.length`); `concurrency` defaults to `1` (sequential) and can be raised when throughput matters. At ~`40` sends/sec, `1M` recipients take ~`7h` — size chunks and checkpoints accordingly.
 *
 * @param ids - Array of user IDs to send the message to.
 *
 * @param languageCode - Array of language codes corresponding to each user.
 *
 * @param keyboard - Optional keyboard markup (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param data - Optional template interpolation data (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - Optional template g-base ID position for block message (or null to use default).
 *
 * @param options - Optional send options (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param throwError - If true, throws errors instead of swallowing them (or null to use false).
 *
 * @param chunkSize - Optional custom chunk size for pacing sleeps (or null for free-limit pacing only).
 *
 * @param chunkDelayMs - Optional delay in ms after each `chunkSize` chunk (or null for `500`).
 *
 * @param excludeIds - Optional user IDs to skip, counted as skipped (or null to send to all).
 *
 * @param onProgress - Optional checkpoint callback `(done, total)` fired after every pacing chunk and once at completion (or null to skip).
 *
 * @param startFrom - Optional absolute recipient index to resume from; indexes below count as skipped and are never resent (or null to start at `0`).
 *
 * @param concurrency - Optional parallel send workers; `1` keeps the sequential loop, floored at `1`, capped at `10`, non-finite becomes `1` (or null for `1`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   const userIds = [123456, 789012]
 *   const langs = [`en`, `id`]
 *   await this.renderBroadcast(userIds, langs)
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Deletes already-sent messages for many recipients in bulk.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Expiry-cleanup counterpart of `renderBroadcastEdit`: same checkpoint-first resume (`startFrom`), bounded-concurrency stride lanes (`concurrency`, capped at `10`), pacing (`30`-message free-limit sleep plus optional `chunkSize`/`chunkDelayMs` sleeps with `onProgress`), and retryable separation (`retryable[]` with absolute `index` + `chatId` + `messageId` + `error`, completion order).
 *
 * Per-recipient failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`: `retryable` errors are recorded and the loop continues; `fallback-text` errors only notify (`notifySendError`) and count as failed. A failed delete has no text fallback by design — there is no replacement content to deliver, so no `sendMessage` is attempted on either path.
 *
 * @param targets - Stored `{chatId, messageId}` rows to delete, in stable order (checkpoint index = array index).
 *
 * @param broadcastOpts - Optional broadcast controls (`onProgress`, `startFrom`, `concurrency`, `chunkSize`, `chunkDelayMs`) (or null for defaults; `fallbackEdit` is accepted but ignored — deletes have no resend).
 *
 * @returns Counts plus `retryable[]` for a re-drive pass.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleExpireVip() {
 *   const sent = await this.db.sentRepo.listByCode(`vip-drop-7`)
 *   await this.renderBroadcastDelete(sent)
 * }

/**
 * Edits already-sent messages for many recipients in bulk.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Mass typo-fix / content-revision counterpart of `renderBroadcastMedia`: same checkpoint-first resume (`startFrom`), bounded-concurrency stride lanes (`concurrency`, capped at `10`), pacing (`30`-message free-limit sleep plus optional `chunkSize`/`chunkDelayMs` sleeps with `onProgress`), retryable separation (`retryable[]` with absolute `index` + `chatId` + `messageId` + `error`, completion order), and fail-fast validation (programmer errors throw BEFORE any send).
 *
 * The intended input source is a stored sent-list such as the downstream `SentRepository` shape (`Array<{chatId, messageId}>` per content code): pass the rows back here to revise the same messages for every recipient.
 *
 * Per-recipient semantics mirror `renderEditMedia` exactly: `photo`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, and `animation` edit in place via `editMessageMedia` (with `InputFile` resolution + filename + caption); `voice`, `video_note`, `sticker`, `location`, and `contact` cannot be edited, so the old message is deleted and a new one is sent; pipe-delimited multi-src media deletes and resends a media group. Every resolved media input is cloned per recipient via `Ctx.cloneMediaInput`, so parallel workers never share one mutable `InputFile` instance.
 *
 * When the primary edit/delete+resend fails, the per-recipient `fallbackEdit` flow runs (default `delete-reply`: best-effort delete, then resend the media without `options1`/`options2`, with a `log.warn` when non-empty edit options are dropped). A failed fallback is classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`: `fallback-text` triggers a best-effort fallback-text send to that recipient (nested failures ignored) and `failedCount++`; `retryable` appends to `retryable[]` and the loop continues. `fallbackEdit: `disable`` skips the resend and classifies the primary error directly.
 *
 * @param targets - Stored `{chatId, messageId}` rows to edit, in stable order (checkpoint index = array index).
 *
 * @param type - The media type (photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact).
 *
 * @param keyboardInline - Optional inline keyboard markup (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param data - Optional template interpolation data (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - Optional template g-base ID position for block media (or null to use default).
 *
 * @param options1 - Type-specific media options (or null to omit; dropped on fallback resend).
 *
 * @param options2 - Additional edit options (or null to omit; dropped on fallback resend).
 *
 * @param broadcastOpts - Optional broadcast controls (`onProgress`, `startFrom`, `concurrency`, `chunkSize`, `chunkDelayMs`, `fallbackEdit`) (or null for defaults).
 *
 * @typeParam T - The media type to edit to.
 *
 * @returns Counts plus `retryable[]` for a re-drive pass.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleTypoFix() {
 *   const sent = await this.db.sentRepo.listByCode(`vip-drop-7`)
 *   await this.renderBroadcastEdit(sent, `photo`, null, {price: `99`})

 * ```

 */

/**

 * @remarks
 *
 * For media types that cannot be edited (voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact), the original message is deleted and a new one is sent. Fail-fast validation runs BEFORE any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.

members.docComment:
/**
 * Sends a template-driven invoice using the page `<g-invoice>` block.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Fail-fast validation (`Ctx.assertInvoice`) runs BEFORE any API call on the COMPILED strings — programmer errors always throw, never fall back. The invoice is sent with NO `parse_mode`: the Bot API offers no HTML parsing for invoices.
 *
 * Provider tokens are security-critical and NEVER come from templates: the validator rejects a `provider_token` attribute outright. Resolution order is `options.provider_token` when present, otherwise Telegram Stars (`currency: "XTR"`) sends with no token at all, and any other (fiat) currency without a token throws before any API call.
 *
 * Pre-checkout queries for the sent invoice already route to page handlers via the existing `precheckoutquery` listener — define `handleFreePreCheckoutQuery` (or `handleSessionFreePreCheckoutQuery` in a session flow) on the page and answer with {@link (Ctx:class).answerPreCheckout}. No new routing was added for this.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `render`): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`). There is no degraded fallback content for invoices, so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched — the `catch` below observes only and never swallows, because swallowing would hide a payment send failure from the caller.
 *
 * @param keyboard - Optional inline keyboard markup from {@link (Ctx:class).inlineKeyboard} (or null to omit). Only inline keyboards are accepted — the Bot API `sendInvoice` reply markup is `InlineKeyboardMarkup`.
 *
 * @param data - Optional template interpolation data (or null to omit).
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - Optional template base ID position for block invoice (or null to use default).
 *
 * @param options - Optional extra `sendInvoice` fields; `provider_token` here is the ONLY way to supply the payment provider secret (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The sent invoice message object.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   const kb = this.inlineKeyboard((k) => k.text("OK", "ok"))
 *   await this.renderInvoice(kb, {days: 30, orderId: "o-1"})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleBuyFiat() {
 *   // Template: <g-invoice title="Pro" description="Plan" payload="{{orderId}}" currency="USD"><g-price label="Pro" amount="499"/></g-invoice>
 *   await this.renderInvoice(null, {orderId: "o-2"}, null, {provider_token: process.env.PAYMENT_PROVIDER_TOKEN})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleFreePreCheckoutQuery() {
 *   await this.answerPreCheckout(true)
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: renderInvoice

members.docComment:
/**
 * Resolve a template media `src` into an uploadable value.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * When `src` points at a real local file (`existsSync` + `statSync().isFile()`), it is wrapped in `new InputFile(src, filename)` so grammy uploads it. `file_id` values, URLs, and missing paths pass through unchanged — never throws. Pre-built `InputFile` instances pass through as-is when no `filename` is given; a defined `filename` returns a prototype-preserving clone (`Object.create` + `Object.assign`) so shared caller instances are never mutated. `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` payloads are wrapped in `new InputFile(src, filename)`.
 *
 * Opt-in local-path jail (Q8 option b): when `roots` is a non-empty list, a local file uploads ONLY when its resolved absolute form sits under one of the resolved roots — otherwise it passes through unchanged (sent as a `file_id`, never throws, never uploads). `null`/empty `roots` keeps current behavior unchanged. `file_id`/URL/`Buffer`/`InputFile` sources are unaffected by the jail. Symlink limitation: the check is lexical (`resolve` without `realpath` — see `Ctx.isPathUnderRoots`).
 *
 * @param src - Template media `src` (file path, `file_id`, URL, or binary payload).
 *
 * @param filename - Optional upload filename; overrides `InputFile.filename` on a clone when defined.
 *
 * @param roots - Optional jail roots; `null`/empty disables the jail.
 *
 * @returns `InputFile` for local files and binary payloads, otherwise `src` unchanged.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: resolveMediaInput

/**
 * Starts a channel giveaway from a single params object.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Data-driven by design (no `<g-giveaway>` block): `sendGiveaway` has no `parse_mode`, so template interpolation adds no value. Requires the bot to be an administrator in the target channel; the installed grammy exposes no typed `sendGiveaway` (neither `api.` nor `api.raw.`), so this validates fail-fast then sends through a structurally-typed raw call (grammy's raw client dispatches any method name at runtime). Fail-fast validation (1+ channels, future integer `date`, positive integer `winners`, non-empty `prize`) runs BEFORE any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back. The first channel receives the giveaway message and doubles as the primary `chats` entry. Channel-targeted by design, so this keeps `api.raw` (context-aware `replyWith*` can only reach the current chat).
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`). There is no degraded fallback content for giveaways, so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * @param params - Giveaway params `{channels, date, winners, prize}` (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param options - Optional giveaway flags such as `onlyNewMembers` (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The sent giveaway message object.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleLaunch() {
 *   await this.startGiveaway({channels: `@mychannel`, date: 1893456000, winners: 2, prize: `iPhone 16`})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: startGiveaway

 * import {Gramstax} from "gramstax"
 *

members.docComment:
/**
 * Routes an incoming update to the appropriate page handler.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The routing follows a strict **priority hierarchy**. When a match is found at any level, the method executes the handler and returns immediately. If no match is found, it falls through to the next level.
 *
 * **Routing Priority (executed in order):**
 *
 * 1. **staticSession** — Session-aware routes, filtered by input type (O(n) lookup) - Only runs when the user has an active session (`session.method` is set) - Iterates `routeStaticSession` and matches by `session.method` value - **Filtered by input type**: only routes whose name ends with `fromListener` are checked (e.g., callback queries only match `*CallbackQueryData` session routes, text only matches `*Text`, photo captions only match `*CaptionPhoto`, etc.) - This prevents cross-type handler misdispatch (e.g., a callback query accidentally matching `handleSessionFreeText`) - Example: session with method "7-mypage" → finds `handleSessionFreeText["7-mypage"]` when `fromListener = "text"`
 *
 * 2. **static** — Exact intent match routes (O(1) lookup) - Matches exact text/callback data to page intents - Example: "start" → `handleText()`, "/help" → `handleCommandText()`
 *
 * 3. **staticIntent** — Intent with args routes (O(1) lookup) - Matches intent prefix when args are present - Example: "start:123" → `handleArgsCallbackQueryData()`, "/add item" → `handleCommandArgsText()`
 *
 * 4. **dynamicSpesific** — Non-session free handlers (O(n) iteration) - Runs all `handleFree*` handlers (defined directly on the page, not inherited) - `handleSessionFree*` variants are NOT dispatched here — they go through id=1 - Example: `handleFreeText()`, `handleFreePhoto()` - **All matching handlers are executed** (no early return)
 *
 * 5. **dynamic** — Global fallback handlers (O(n) iteration) - Runs all `handleFree()` handlers from pages that define them - Last resort when nothing else matches - **All matching handlers are executed** (no early return)
 *
 * @param ctx - The context instance.
 *
 * @param fromListener - The listener type that triggered the route.
 *
 * @returns A `PageRouteResult` with `state` indicating what happened
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _pageRoutes

members.docComment:
/**
 * Creates a new Gramstax bot instance.
 *
 * @param params - Configuration options. See {@link ITGramstaxParams} for all available options.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Polling mode (development, local testing)
 * new Gramstax({token: "BOT_TOKEN", deploy: "polling"})
 *
 * // Webhook mode with Bun's HTTP server
 * new Gramstax({token: "BOT_TOKEN", deploy: "webhook:https://example.com/bot"})
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — Bun std/http adapter
 * //
 * // The bot does NOT self-host; instead it sets up handlerBotUpdate
 * // for your serverless runtime. Export the handler and let your
 * // platform invoke it per HTTP request.
 *
 * // bot.ts — instantiation
 * const bot = new Gramstax({
 *   token: process.env.BOT_TOKEN!,
 *   deploy: "serverless:std/http"
 * })
 *
 * // handler.ts — server entry point
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 *
 * // Bun's built-in HTTP server
 * Bun.serve({
 *   port: 3000,
 *   async fetch(req) {
 *     const url = new URL(req.url)
 *     if (url.pathname === "/webhook") {
 *       // Forward the request to gramstax's handler
 *       return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(req)
 *     }
 *     return new Response("Not found", {status: 404})
 *   }
 * })
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — AWS Lambda
 * //
 * // bot.ts
 * const bot = new Gramstax({
 *   token: process.env.BOT_TOKEN!,
 *   deploy: "serverless:aws-lambda"
 * })
 *
 * // lambda.ts
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 * import type {APIGatewayProxyEvent, Context} from "aws-lambda"
 *
 * export const handler = async (event: APIGatewayProxyEvent, _ctx: Context) => {
 *   // webhookCallback(bot.bot, "aws-lambda") wraps the raw event
 *   // into a compatible format internally
 *   return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(event)
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — Cloudflare Workers
 * //
 * // bot.ts
 * const bot = new Gramstax({token: env.BOT_TOKEN, deploy: "serverless:cloudflare-workers-mod"})
 *
 * // worker.ts
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 *
 * export default {
 *   async fetch(request: Request) {
 *     const url = new URL(request.url)
 *     if (url.pathname === "/webhook") {
 *       return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(request)
 *     }
 *     return new Response("OK")
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

 * Only assembly point for `createCtx`: per-update `ct` plus the constructor-built `ctxScope` plus a fresh `temp`. App values (e.g. a database handle) ride in `extra` through the params object, but the `Ctx` constructor does NOT attach them — assign each one explicitly in your subclass constructor so every wiring stays visible and easy to troubleshoot. `extra` keys must not be `ct`/`temp` (thrown here).
 *
 * @param ct - The grammy context for the current update.
 *
 * @param extra - Optional app values forwarded into every page `Ctx`.
 *
 * @typeParam T - App extra fields merged into the returned params.
 *
 * @returns Params for `new Ctx(...)`, shaped as `ITCtxParams & T`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   db = new Db()
 *   override buildCtxParams<T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, never>>(ct: ITCt, _extra?: T): ITCtxParams & T & {db: Db} {
 *     return super.buildCtxParams(ct, {db: this.db}) as ITCtxParams & T & {db: Db}
 *   }
 * }
 * class CtxCore extends Ctx {
 *   declare db: Db
 *   constructor(params: ITCtxParams & {db: Db}) {
 *     super(params)
 *     this.db = params.db
 *   }
 * }
 * // inside any page extending CtxCore: this.db — fully typed, zero casts.
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: buildCtxParams

/**
 * Hook called before the bot starts.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Override this method to run **one-off initialization logic** that must complete before the bot begins dispatching updates — for example, connecting to a database, warming a cache, validating external service credentials, or setting up shared singletons that pages will read from.
 *
 * This hook fires exactly once, after `cacheSession`, `templateManager`, `bot`, and `pages` are initialized, and before polling/webhook/serverless actually begins receiving updates.
 *
 * **Do NOT register middleware here.** Middleware belongs in {@link Gramstax.registerLowPlugin}, which is the dedicated channel for code that should run on every incoming update. `hookBeforeStart` runs once and is the wrong place for per-update logic.
 *
 * For background tasks that need the bot to be alive (cron jobs, periodic cleanup, queue processors), use {@link Gramstax.hookAfterStart} instead.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   async hookBeforeStart() {
 *     // Validate external service credentials before the bot goes live
 *     if (!process.env.REDIS_URL) {
 *       throw new Error(`REDIS_URL is required`)
 *     }
 *     this.log?.info?.(`Verifying external service connection...`)
 *     await pingRedis(process.env.REDIS_URL)
 *     this.log?.success?.(`External services ready`)
 *   }
 * }
 * ```

 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookBeforeStart

members.docComment:
/**
 * Best-effort send-error hook.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Sibling hooks: `hookUpdateError` (dead updates — terminal) and `hookTrace` (every routed update). This one is the recoverable layer: a `fallback-text` send still serves the user, a `retryable` send still throws to your caller. Routing rule: retry-queue ← `hookSendError`, Sentry ← `hookUpdateError`, dashboard ← `hookTrace`.
 *
 * @param err - The send error.
 *
 * @param info - The send-error info (`page`, `kind`, `chatId`). See {@link ITSendErrorHook}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ITSendErrorInfo): void {
 *     // info: {page: `admin/logs`, kind: `fallback-text` | `retryable`, chatId?: number}
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) queueRetry(info)
 *     else metrics.count(info.page, info.kind)
 *   }
 * }
 * // Throwing inside the hook is swallowed — the send flow never breaks.
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Retry-for-later: collect retryables, re-drive them from a job.
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   retryQueue: Array<{err: unknown, page: string, chatId?: number, at: number}> = []
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ITSendErrorInfo): void {
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) this.retryQueue.push({err, page: info.page, chatId: info.chatId, at: Date.now()})
 *   }
 * }
 * // NOTE: `retryable` still throws to your caller — the hook only observes.
 * // Drain `retryQueue` from a worker/job; do not retry inline (429 needs backoff).
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Severity split: Sentry for retryables, logs for user-caused fallbacks.
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ITSendErrorInfo): void {
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) Sentry.captureException(err, {tags: {page: info.page}})
 *     // `fallback-text` (403 blocked, file deleted) is a normal condition — log, don't alert.
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @defaultValue `undefined` (no hook)
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookSendError

members.docComment:

 * Optional OTel-style trace export hook.

members.docComment:
/**
 * Returns middleware to register as low-level plugins on the bot.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Override this method in a subclass to inject custom plugin middleware (sessions, i18n, rate limiting, logging, authentication, etc.) into the underlying bot instance.
 *
 * Each element of the returned array is a {@link ITCtMiddleware} value (either a `MiddlewareFn` `(ctx, next) => ...` or a `MiddlewareObj` container) that The array elements are passed to `this.bot.use(...)`. It is meant to be spread into `bot.use`, so the order of elements determines the order in which middleware runs — earlier entries wrap later ones (outermost first).
 *
 * Difference vs. the other lifecycle hooks:
 *
 * - `hookBeforeStart` — for one-off side effects before the bot starts. Anything you want to happen exactly once at boot goes there. - `registerLowPlugin` — for middleware that must run on **every update**. Use this when you need middleware semantics (filter queries, `next()` chaining, scope-aware registration). - `hookBeforeRoute` / `hookAfterRoute` — for per-update hooks that run inside the router, after gramstax has already routed to a page.
 *
 * The base implementation is not provided — subclasses override this to contribute their own plugins. Returning an empty array (or not overriding) installs no plugins, which is the default behavior.
 *
 * @returns Array of {@link ITCtMiddleware} values, ready to be spread into `this.bot.use(...result)`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   registerLowPlugin() {
 *     return [
 *       // 1. Logging middleware (outermost — runs first, exits last)
 *       async (ctx, next) => {
 *         this.log?.info?.(`update ${ctx.update.update_id} from ${ctx.from?.id}`)
 *         await next()
 *       },
 *       // 2. Per-chat rate limit (inner)
 *       async (ctx, next) => {
 *         // ... check + throttle ...
 *         await next()
 *       }
 *     ]
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: registerLowPlugin

/**

 * @remarks
 *
 * Full page data with typed `callbackQueryData` according to the args configured via `buildData`. Every page SHOULD define `static data` via `buildData(...)` to enable callback query routing.
 *
 * - `buildData()` (no args) → `callbackQueryData(): {result, page, args: []}` — 0 args only - `buildData((a: string, b: string) => ...)` → `callbackQueryData(a, b): {result, page, args: [a, b]}` - `buildData((a?: string) => ...)` → `callbackQueryData(a?): {result, page, args}` (optional still supported)

 * The page class is NOT carried by `static data` (TS cannot infer it without a circular annotation) — pass it explicitly when you want route validation: `Page.data.callbackQueryData<Page>("42")` is compile-error checked against `handleArgsCallbackQueryData`; without the type argument the object is accepted as-is and the route is only resolved at runtime.

/**
 * Synchronously load all page modules from a directory.

 * Supports both flat `.ts`/`.js` files and subfolder `index.ts`/`index.js` entries. In a subfolder, **any** `.ts`/`.js` file (not just `index`) is recognised as a page — its route name becomes `parentDir/basename`. A file `help.ts` is equivalent to `help/index.ts`; using both simultaneously produces a duplicate error. Nesting can be arbitrary deep.
 *
 * Supported cases and extensions: - Extensions: `.ts` and `.js` only — other files are ignored. - Flat file: `start.ts` → route `start`. - Nested file: `admin/ban.ts` → route `admin/ban` (arbitrary depth). - Directory index: `admin/index.ts` → route `admin`. - A root-level `index.ts`/`index.js` has no parent route and is rejected with an empty-routeName error — rename it to a named file instead.

 * //   { path: "/path/to/settings.ts",       page: SettingsPage, routeName: "settings" },
 * //   { path: "/path/to/start/help.ts",     page: HelpPage,    routeName: "start/help" },

/**
 * Static utility class for parsing and compiling HTML-like templates.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The `TemplateEngine` provides methods for parsing HTML-like template syntax with custom blocks (base, message, keyboard, media, description, etc.) and compiling them into executable functions. It supports variable interpolation, conditional rendering, array mapping, script execution, and template imports.
 *
 * Templates are typically organized into `<g-base>` blocks containing various content blocks like `<g-message>`, `<g-keyboard>`, `<g-media>`, and `<g-description>`. Each block supports a `lang` attribute for internationalization.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { TemplateEngine } from 'gramstax';
 *
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-keyboard>Back, Next</g-keyboard>
 *     <g-message>Welcome {{name}}!</g-message>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 *
 * const messages = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGMessages(template);
 * const keyboards = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGKeyboards(template);
 *
 * const msg = messages.default?.default?.({ name: 'John' });
 * // Result: 'Welcome John!'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: TemplateEngine

 *
 * @param rawSrc - Raw `src` attribute value from the parsed template.

 * @param stringFn - Existing compiled string renderer for this `src`.

/**
 * Escapes special characters in a string for safe use in template literals.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method escapes backslashes, backticks, and `${` sequences to prevent static template text from breaking out of template literal syntax during compilation. Applied to static segments before they are embedded in generated code (`_compileToFunction` builds concatenation, never raw backtick-wrapped statics; block processors escape embedded content).
 *
 * @param str - The input string to escape
 *
 * @returns The escaped string with backslashes and backticks properly escaped
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const escaped = TemplateEngine._escape('Hello `world`');
 * // Result: 'Hello \\`world\\`'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escape

 * HTML-escapes a runtime value for safe interpolation into rich-HTML messages.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Non-string values are stringified; `null`/`undefined` become empty string. Escaped code points: `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`. Scope: text-node interpolation via `{{}}` only. Attribute values and `{{{}}}` raw output are intentionally not HTML-escaped.
 *
 * @param value - The runtime value to escape.
 *
 * @returns The escaped string.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escapeData

members.docComment:
/**
 * Escapes static template text while preserving template syntax spans.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Walks `content` char-by-char: `{{{...}}}`, `{{...}}`, and `{~...~}` spans pass through untouched (they are converted to generated code later). A balanced `${...}` span is preserved live only when its inner code passes {@link TemplateEngine._isGeneratedCode} — i.e. it was produced by an inner block processor (nested `<g-map>` bodies carry `${(() => ...)}` / `${__esc(...)}` spans through outer escaping). Any other `${` sequence (untrusted/static text, unterminated spans) is neutralized via {@link TemplateEngine._escape}, consistent with top-level static text. Every other character goes through {@link TemplateEngine._escape}, neutralizing breakout payloads (backticks, backslashes) in untrusted static text. Used by `_processGSwitchBlocks` and `_processGMapBlocks` for case/default and loop bodies.
 *
 * @param content - Raw static block content to escape.
 *
 * @returns The content with non-syntax characters escaped.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escapeStaticExceptInterpolation

members.docComment:
/**
 * Extracts specific blocks from template content with optional filtering.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method extracts content from templates based on base ID, block type, language, and section mode. It supports scoped extraction with indentation normalization for clean output.
 *
 * @param content - The template content to extract from
 *
 * @param blocks - Block type(s) to extract, or `"all"` for all blocks
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - The base ID to extract from (defaults to `"default"`)
 *
 * @param section - Whether to return the full block (`"all"`) or just inner content (`"value"`)
 *
 * @param lang - Optional language filter for blocks
 *
 * @returns The extracted content as a string
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript

/**
 * Compiles a processed template string into an executable function.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method takes a pre-processed template (or array of templates) and compiles it into a JavaScript function that accepts a `data` object and returns the rendered result. The function is created using `new Function()`. Static segments are emitted via string concatenation (`JSON.stringify` literals joined with `+`), never wrapped in a raw backtick literal, so static backticks, backslashes, and `${` sequences cannot break out into code. Only `${...}` spans produced by the block/scope processors are evaluated.

 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const processed = '${(data && data["name"]) ?? ""}';
 * const fn = TemplateEngine._compileToFunction(processed, false);

 * ```

 */

members.docComment:
/**
 * Attribute value validators for `<g-*>` PAGE blocks.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Per-tag, per-attribute map of validators. Each validator receives the raw attribute value (after quote-stripping) and returns either `null` (valid) or a descriptive error string. The value validation runs after the per-block attribute validation, so unknown attributes are reported separately by `validateBlockG*Attributes` methods.
 *
 * Currently covers: - `<g-base id>` — must not be empty - `<g-keyboard type>` — must be `inline` or `bottom` - `<g-media type>` — must be one of: photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact - `<g-media shared>` — must be `true` or `false` - `<g-media filename>` — any string, always valid - `<g-poll type>` — must be `regular` or `quiz` - `<g-poll correct>` — must be a non-negative option index - `<g-poll explanation>` — any string, always valid - `<g-poll anonymous>` / `<g-poll multiple>` — must be `true` or `false` - `<g-venue title>` / `<g-venue address>` — any string, always valid - `<g-venue latitude>` — must be a number between -90 and 90; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-venue longitude>` — must be a number between -180 and 180; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-dice emoji>` — must be one of 🎲🎯🏀⚽🎳🎰; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-invoice currency>` — must be a 3-letter code (`XTR` or fiat); `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-price amount>` — must be a positive integer in smallest currency units - `<g-paid-media stars>` — must be a positive integer 1–25000; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 *
 * Validators are intentionally lenient — they catch obvious bugs (wrong type, invalid value) but do not enforce every framework-level constraint.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * TemplateEngine._PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS["g-keyboard"].type("inline")   // => null
 * TemplateEngine._PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS["g-keyboard"].type("sidebar") // => "Attribute \"type\" on <g-keyboard> must be \"inline\" or \"bottom\", got \"sidebar\""
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS

members.docComment:
/**
 * Block: g-media Extracts and parses `<g-media>` blocks from a template string.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method identifies all `<g-media>` blocks and extracts their attributes and content. It supports various media types including photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, and contact. The inner content becomes the caption for supported types.
 *
 * **Attributes:** - `lang` (optional): Language key for the output map. Defaults to `"default"`. - `type` (required): Media type discriminator. Expected values: - `photo`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `animation`, `voice`, `video_note`, - `sticker`, `location`, `contact`. - `src` (optional): File path / URL / file identifier for file-based media. - `latitude` (optional): Location latitude (used when `type="location"`). - `longitude` (optional): Location longitude (used when `type="location"`). - `phone` (optional): Contact phone number (used when `type="contact"`). - `first_name` (optional): Contact first name (used when `type="contact"`). - `last_name` (optional): Contact last name (used when `type="contact"`). - `vcard` (optional): Contact vCard payload (used when `type="contact"`).
 *
 * Media rules (based on `type`): - If `src` exists, it is assigned as `mediaBlock.src` (for any type). - If `src` contains pipe-delimited values, `mediaBlock.srcList` is populated with up to 10 trimmed entries for Telegram media groups. - If caption exists and `type !== "video_note"` and `type !== "sticker"`, it is assigned as `mediaBlock.caption`. - If `type === "location"`, `latitude` and `longitude` are copied if present, and caption (if present) is also allowed. - If `type === "contact"`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`, and `vcard` are copied if present, and caption (if present) is also allowed.
 *
 * Note: - If multiple `<g-media>` blocks share the same `lang`, the last one wins (it overwrites the previous entry).
 *
 * @param template - The template string containing `<g-media>` blocks
 *
 * @returns An object mapping language keys to their corresponding media block configurations
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = '<g-media type="photo" src="image.jpg|image-2.jpg" lang="en">Hello</g-media>';
 * const media = TemplateEngine._processGMediaBlocks(template);
 * // Result: { en: { type: 'photo', src: 'image.jpg|image-2.jpg', srcList: ['image.jpg', 'image-2.jpg'], caption: 'Hello' } }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _processGMediaBlocks

 * const processed = TemplateEngine._processExec(template);
 * // Result: 'Total: ${(() => { try { return data?.count ?? 0 } catch(e) { try { with(data || {}) { return data?.count ?? 0 } } catch(ee) { return '' } } })()}'

/**
 * Scope: `{{}}` Converts `{{variable}}` placeholders to JavaScript template literal expressions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method transforms Mustache-like variable syntax into JavaScript template literal interpolation. `{{key}}` is HTML-escaped at runtime; `{{{key}}}` is inserted raw. Variables are accessed from the `data` object, with nullish coalescing to empty string when undefined. Surrounding whitespace inside the braces is trimmed. Each filter segment splits its name on the first `:` only; the remainder is passed as one combined argument (so `date:HH:mm:ss` stays whole; `plural` splits its combined `one:many` argument itself). Filter arguments are embedded via `JSON.stringify`, never raw backticks. Unknown filter warnings are deduplicated per compile call; other expressions in the same template still render (unknown one renders empty).

 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const processed = TemplateEngine._processScopeVariables('Hello {{name}}!');
 * // Result: 'Hello ${__esc((data && data["name"]) ?? "")}!'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Compiles description blocks from a template into executable functions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method parses `<g-description>` blocks from the template and compiles them into functions that generate rendered description strings. The result is organized by base ID, scope, and language. Used for Telegram bot command descriptions.
 *
 * Processing pipeline (in order, per description): 1. `_processGScriptBlocks` – converts `<g-script>` blocks into executable expressions 2. `_processGMapBlocks` – converts `<g-map>` blocks into array map expressions 3. `_processGSwitchBlocks` – converts `<g-switch>` blocks into switch expressions 4. `_processScopeExec` – evaluates scope execution blocks (implementation-defined) 5. `_processScopeVariables` – resolves scope variables (implementation-defined) 6. `_compileToFunction(processed, false)` – produces the final render function
 *
 * Output shape: - First level key: `AGBaseId` (from `<g-base id="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted) - Second level key: `AScope` (from `<g-description scope="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted) - Third level key: `ALang` (from `<g-description lang="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted) - Value: `(data?: Record<string, unknown>) => string`
 *
 * @param template - Raw template string containing `<g-base>` and `<g-description>` blocks
 *
 * @param gBaseBlocks - Optional pre-parsed base blocks for reuse
 *
 * @returns Compiled description functions organized by base ID, scope, and language
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-description>Start the bot</g-description>
 *     <g-description scope="chat_administrators">Admin command</g-description>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 * const descriptions = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGDescription(template);
 * const result = descriptions.default?.default?.default?.({});
 * // Result: 'Start the bot'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: compileBlockGDescription

/**
 * Compiles message blocks from a template into executable functions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method parses `<g-message>` blocks from the template and compiles them into functions that generate rendered message strings. The result is organized by base ID and language. Pre-parsed base blocks can be provided for efficiency.
 *
 * Processing pipeline (in order, per message): 1. `_processGScriptBlocks` - converts `<g-script>` blocks into executable expressions 2. `_processGMapBlocks` - converts `<g-map>` blocks into array map expressions 3. `_processGSwitchBlocks` - converts `<g-switch>` blocks into switch expressions 4. `_processScopeExec` - evaluates scope execution blocks (implementation-defined) 5. `_processScopeVariables` - resolves scope variables (implementation-defined) 6. `_compileToFunction(processed, false)` - produces the final render function
 *
 * Output shape: - First level key: `AGBaseId` (from `<g-base id="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted) - Second level key: `ALang` (from `<g-message lang="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted) - Value: `(data?: Record<string, unknown>) => string`
 *
 * @param template - Raw template string containing `<g-base>` and `<g-message>` blocks
 *
 * @param baseBlocks - Optional pre-parsed base blocks for reuse
 *
 * @returns Compiled message functions organized by base ID and language
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-message>Hello {{name}}!</g-message>
 *     <g-message lang="id">Halo {{name}}!</g-message>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 * const messages = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGMessages(template);
 * const result = messages.default?.default?.({ name: 'John' });
 * // Result: 'Hello John!'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: compileBlockGMessage

/**
 * Recursively processes and resolves `<g-import>` blocks in a template.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method resolves all `<g-import>` placeholders produced by `_processGImportBlocks` by invoking a user-provided `resolver` function.
 *
 * Resolution behavior: - Each `<g-import>` is resolved by calling `resolver(src)` to obtain raw template content. - The resolved content is filtered using `_extractBlock` based on the import metadata (`blocks`, `base`, `section`, `lang`). - If the resolved content itself contains `<g-import>` directives, they are processed recursively.
 *
 * Recursion and safety: - Recursive import resolution is limited to a maximum depth of **10** to prevent infinite import loops. - If the depth limit is exceeded, an empty string is returned.
 *
 * Output behavior: - `<g-import>` placeholders (`__IMPORT_N__`) are replaced sequentially. - If the resolver returns `null` or an empty result, the import is replaced with an empty string.
 *
 * @param template - Template string containing `<g-import>` directives
 *
 * @param resolver - Function that resolves import sources to template content
 *
 * @param depth - Current recursion depth (defaults to 0)
 *
 * @param importCache - Optional Map to cache resolved imports for reuse
 *
 * @returns Template with all `<g-import>` blocks resolved and replaced
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = '<g-import src="header" block="message" />\n<g-message>Main content</g-message>';
 * const resolver = (src: string) => {
 *   if (src === 'header') return '<g-message>Header text</g-message>';
 *   return null;
 * };
 * const result = TemplateEngine.processGImportBlocks(template, resolver);
 * // Result: '<g-message>Header text</g-message>\n<g-message>Main content</g-message>'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: processGImportBlocks

/**
 * Validates that `<g-*>` PAGE block attribute values match their expected formats.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Runs after `TemplateEngine.validateBlockG*Attributes` (which check allowed attrs) to catch format-level issues. Currently validates: - `<g-base id>` — must not be empty - `<g-keyboard type>` — must be `inline` or `bottom` - `<g-media type>` — must be one of: photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact - `<g-media shared>` — must be `true` or `false` - `<g-media filename>` — any string, always valid - `<g-poll type>` — must be `regular` or `quiz` - `<g-poll correct>` — must be a non-negative option index - `<g-poll explanation>` — any string, always valid - `<g-poll anonymous>` / `<g-poll multiple>` — must be `true` or `false` - `<g-venue title>` / `<g-venue address>` — any string, always valid - `<g-venue latitude>` — must be a number between -90 and 90; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-venue longitude>` — must be a number between -180 and 180; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-dice emoji>` — must be one of 🎲🎯🏀⚽🎳🎰; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-invoice currency>` — must be a 3-letter code (`XTR` or fiat); `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced) - `<g-price amount>` — must be a positive integer in smallest currency units - `<g-paid-media stars>` — must be a positive integer 1–25000; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 *
 * Tags without value validators (e.g. `<g-message>`, `<g-script>`, `<g-div>`) are skipped. See {@link TemplateEngine._PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS} for the full spec.
 *
 * @param template - The raw template string to validate
 *
 * @returns An object with a `valid` boolean and an `errors` array
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const result = TemplateEngine.validatePageAttributeValuesBlock(`
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-keyboard type="inline">A, B</g-keyboard>
 *   </g-base>
 * `);
 * // Result: { valid: true, errors: [] }
 *
 * const bad = TemplateEngine.validatePageAttributeValuesBlock(`
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-keyboard type="sidebar">A, B</g-keyboard>
 *   </g-base>
 * `);
 * // Result: { valid: false, errors: [{ line: 3, message: 'Attribute "type" on <g-keyboard> must be "inline" or "bottom", got "sidebar"' }] }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: validatePageAttributeValuesBlock

members.docComment:
/**
 * Validates block positioning and nesting rules in a template string.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method checks a template string for structural block nesting violations. It ensures that blocks are placed in their allowed parent contexts.
 *
 * **Nesting hierarchy:**
 * ```
 * __root__
 *   ├── g-base             (root level only)
 *   │   ├── g-message      (content block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-switch   (logic block)
 *   │   │   │   ├── case
 *   │   │   │   └── default
 *   │   │   ├── g-map      (logic block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-script   (logic block)
 *   │   │   └── g-space    (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-keyboard     (content block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-switch   (logic block)
 *   │   │   │   ├── g-case
 *   │   │   │   └── g-default
 *   │   │   ├── g-map      (logic block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-script   (logic block)
 *   │   │   └── g-space    (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-media        (content block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-switch   (logic block)
 *   │   │   │   ├── g-case
 *   │   │   │   └── g-default
 *   │   │   ├── g-map      (logic block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-script   (logic block)
 *   │   │   └── g-space    (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-description  (content block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-switch   (logic block)
 *   │   │   │   ├── g-case
 *   │   │   │   └── g-default
 *   │   │   ├── g-map      (logic block)
 *   │   │   ├── g-script   (logic block)
 *   │   │   └── g-space    (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-import       (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-description  (utility)
 *   │   ├── g-script       (logic block)
 *   └   └── g-space        (utility)
 * ```
 *
 * **Enforced rules:** - `<g-base>` must be at the outermost level and cannot be nested inside any other block. - `<g-message>`, `<g-keyboard>`, `<g-media>`, `<g-media-group>`, `<g-poll>`, `<g-invoice>`, `<g-paid-media>`, `<g-venue>`, `<g-dice>`, `<g-description>`, `<g-import>`, `<g-script>`, `<g-space>` can only appear directly inside `<g-base>`. - `<g-media>` can also appear directly inside `<g-media-group>` as a group item, or inside `<g-paid-media>` as a paywall item. - `<g-question>` and `<g-option>` can only appear directly inside `<g-poll>`. - `<g-price>` can only appear directly inside `<g-invoice>`. - `<g-switch>`, `<g-map>` can only appear inside `<g-message>`, `<g-keyboard>`, `<g-media>`, or `<g-description>`. - `<g-case>` and `<g-default>` can only appear inside `<g-switch>`. - `<g-map>` is also allowed inside `<g-case>` and `<g-default>` (explicitly and via parent-child inheritance — see `inheritsContentFromParent`). - Telegram formatting tags (`<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>`, `<s>`, `<code>`, `<pre>`, `<a>`, `<blockquote>`, `<blockquote expandable>`) are passthrough and ignored during validation.
 *
 * @param template - The raw template string to validate
 *
 * @returns An object with a `valid` boolean and an `errors` array containing line numbers and descriptive messages for each violation found
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Valid template
 * const result = TemplateEngine.validatePositionsBlock(`
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-message>Hello {{name}}!</g-message>
 *     <g-keyboard>Yes, No</g-keyboard>
 *   </g-base>
 * `);
 * // Result: { valid: true, errors: [] }
 *
 * // Invalid: <g-base> nested inside <g-message>
 * const bad = TemplateEngine.validatePositionsBlock(`
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-message>
 *       <g-base>Nested base</g-base>
 *     </g-message>
 *   </g-base>
 * `);
 * // Result: { valid: false, errors: [{ line: 4, message: 'Block <g-base> is not allowed inside <g-message>' }] }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: validatePositionsBlock

/**

 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Executes every registered validator in sequence and collects all errors. Validation steps:
 *
 * 1. {@link TemplateEngine.validateNamesBlock} — checks that all tags are known 2. {@link TemplateEngine.validateScopes} — checks that all interpolation scopes are known 3. {@link TemplateEngine.validateFormatBlock} — checks self-closing vs regular tag syntax 4. {@link TemplateEngine.validatePositionsBlock} — checks structural nesting rules 5. {@link TemplateEngine.validateTelegramAttributesBlock} — checks required attributes on Telegram Rich HTML tags 6. {@link TemplateEngine.validateTelegramAttributeValuesBlock} — checks value formats on Telegram Rich HTML tag attributes 7. {@link TemplateEngine.validateTelegramUnknownAttributesBlock} — rejects unknown attribute names on Telegram Rich HTML tags 8. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGBaseAttributes} — checks `<g-base>` block attributes 9. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGMessageAttributes} — checks `<g-message>` block attributes 10. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGKeyboardAttributes} — checks `<g-keyboard>` block attributes 11. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGMediaAttributes} — checks `<g-media>` block attributes 12. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGMediaGroupAttributes} — checks `<g-media-group>` block attributes 13. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGPollAttributes} — checks `<g-poll>` block attributes 14. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGDescriptionAttributes} — checks `<g-description>` block attributes 15. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGScriptAttributes} — checks `<g-script>` block attributes 16. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGSwitchAttributes} — checks `<g-switch>` block attributes 17. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGCaseAttributes} — checks `<g-case>` block attributes 18. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGDefaultAttributes} — checks `<g-default>` block attributes 19. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGMapAttributes} — checks `<g-map>` block attributes 20. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGDivAttributes} — checks `<g-div>` block attributes 21. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGImportAttributes} — checks `<g-import>` block attributes 22. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGSpaceAttributes} — checks `<g-space>` block attributes 23. {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGVenueAttributes} — checks `<g-venue>` block attributes 24. {@link /**
 * Manages template loading, compilation, caching, and hot-reloading from page files.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The `TemplateManager` class provides a centralized system for handling templates used in Gramstax bots. It supports: - Loading templates from static `template` properties in page classes - Loading templates from external `.html` files - Hot-reloading templates during development via file watching - Multi-language support with fallback to `default`
 *
 * Templates are compiled once and cached for efficient retrieval.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import {TemplateManager} from "gramstax"
 * import {join} from "path"
 *
 * const tm = new TemplateManager({
 *   path: [join(process.cwd(), "src", "pages")],
 *   enableWatch: process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"
 * })
 *
 * // Get a compiled message
 * const message = tm.getMessage("start", "default", "en", {name: "John"})
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: TemplateManager

members.docComment:
/**
 * Validates template syntax and throws a descriptive error on failure.
 *
 * The error message includes the enclosing `<g-base id="...">` based on the error line. If the `<g-base>` has no `id` or no `<g-base>` tag is found, the `on base` prefix is omitted.
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - Cache key (filename without extension), used as default filename
 *
 * @param template - Template content to validate
 *
 * @param filename - Source filename with extension, shown in error location
 *
 * @throws
 *
 * Error with format: `Template on base "${id}" (file, line X): msg` or `Template (file, line X): msg`
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // base with id:
 * this._validateTemplate("start", '<g-base id="kb"><kop/></g-base>', "start.html")
 * // => throws: Template on base "kb" (start.html, line 1): Unsupported template block: <kop>
 *
 * // base without id:
 * this._validateTemplate("start", '<g-base><kop/></g-base>', "start.html")
 * // => throws: Template (start.html, line 1): Unsupported template block: <kop>
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _validateTemplate
